title: How targeting cash transfers at women strengthens bargaining power within the household
summary: In Mexico, income transfers targeted at women are effective at improving their decision-making position within the household, translating into significant changes in household consumption and time allocation patterns.

title: When microfinance credit contracted in India, children’s education suffered
summary: In Andhra Pradesh, credit contraction in the rural economy, triggered by microfinance regulation, lowered educational investments and caused lasting learning losses, with larger effects for girls and younger children.

title: Why railways alone don’t drive development

summary: Mamo Mihretu on export-led manufacturing, economic reform and the macroeconomic foundations of a growing economy.

title: The long shadow of the 1997 financial crisis in Thailand
summary: The 1997 Thai financial crisis had far longer lasting consequences for financial access than aggregate measures suggest, driven by bank branch closures that were never reversed even after the broader economy recovered.

title: An improved nighttime-lights dataset for development research
summary: A new adjusted and harmonised satellite nighttime-lights series for 1992–2023 tracks local development in the Global South more accurately than the off-the-shelf data – especially in panels and at fine spatial resolution.

title: Monitoring markets from space

title: Decentralising development: The economic effects of government splits
summary: When Brazil let neglected districts break away and form new municipalities, peripheral areas gained services, jobs, and growth at no visible cost to the rest of the country.
